newsitem.title: ABU DHABI: UAE threatens tough measures against arms violators.
newsitem.headline: UAE threatens tough measures against arms violators.

text.p: The UAE said on Wednesday it would halt business with a country's arms exporters if one of the country's firms reneges on agreements signed with the Gulf Arab state.

Colonel Obeid al-Kitbi, the UAE deputy director general of arms procurements, told a news conference at Abu Dhabi's IDEX arms show that his country's decision on Tuesday to halt deals with any Italian firm due to a dispute with Italy's BPD Difesa e Spazio (Fiat Avio Group) could apply elsewhere.

Asked if the UAE would take similar moves against companies from countries such as the United States, France and China in the event of a similar dispute with a firm, he said: "Somebody really failed to fulfill his commitment. That will be applied to whoever makes the mistake."
"We are talking about contractual commitments. Whoever fails to fulfill that, the same thing will be applied. Any country," he added.
Kitbi announced the move against Italian arms firms on Tuesday after his country failed to resolve a dispute over rocket launchers with BPD, running since 1994.
The UAE, a prized player in the international arms market, withdrew the Italian-made rapid launcher rocket system from military use in 1996 due to a recurring technical malfunction.
The 24 multiple launchers and thousands of surface-to-surface rockets, with a 30-km (19 miles) range, were bought in the 1980s for $280 million, officials said. The problem did not appear until 1994.
